title: JANUS Linear A SigLA-native blind word-boundary role discovery
research_question: Do any repeated SigLA-native word identities, represented only by standard sign-ID sequences, reproducibly specialize for document-initial or document-final word position more strongly than within-document identity-shuffle nulls predict?

source.name: SigLA — The Signs of Linear A

blind_representation.candidate_identity: SHA256('SIGLA-WORD-v0.1|' + exact SigLA seq-pattern sign-ID sequence)
scoring_uses: location only for final support gate
blind_representation.zero_word_and_singleton_documents: retained in parser audit; only documents with >=2 parsed words enter INITIAL/FINAL role statistics

screen_gate.effect: observed role fraction minus mean null role fraction
screen_gate.multiplicity: Bonferroni over all eligible candidate×role hypotheses

parser_fail_closed.word_sequence_extraction: Only search-sequence anchors with explicit word-match @ !seq-pattern:{...}// are scientific words.
parser_fail_closed.word_count_consistency: If reported word count differs from extracted seq-pattern count, document is excluded and recorded as parser mismatch.

claim_ceiling.forbidden: Any translation/lexical meaning claim from positional specialization alone.

roadmap_after_execution.if_full_survivor: Post-score literature novelty audit, mwenge cross-encoding comparison, behavioral/document-role audit, then independently implemented replay.
roadmap_after_execution.if_known_survivor: Register blind rediscovery as positive control and subtract known family in a separately frozen follow-up.
roadmap_after_execution.if_no_survivor: Preserve valid negative result and move to SigLA-native sign-within-word morphology / formula-neighborhood channel without lowering thresholds.
